scene.label: Act 4, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. London. Before the Tower

content.text: Enter Queen Elizabeth, the Duchess of York and Marquess of Dorset, at one door; Anne Duchess of Gloucester with Clarence's young Daughter at another door.

lines.text: Who meets us here? My niece Plantagenet
lines.plainText: Who meets us here My niece Plantagenet

lines.text: Led in the hand of her kind aunt of Gloucester?
lines.plainText: Led in the hand of her kind aunt of Gloucester

lines.text: Now, for my life, she's wandering to the Tower,
lines.plainText: Now for my life she's wandering to the Tower

lines.text: On pure heart's love, to greet the tender Prince.
lines.plainText: On pure heart's love to greet the tender Prince

lines.text: Daughter, well met.
lines.plainText: Daughter well met

lines.text: God give your Graces both
lines.plainText: God give your Graces both

lines.text: A happy and a joyful time of day.
lines.plainText: A happy and a joyful time of day

lines.text: As much to you, good sister. Whither away?
lines.plainText: As much to you good sister Whither away

lines.text: No farther than the Tower, and, as I guess,
lines.plainText: No farther than the Tower and as I guess

lines.text: Upon the like devotion as yourselves,
lines.plainText: Upon the like devotion as yourselves

lines.text: To gratulate the gentle Princes there.
lines.plainText: To gratulate the gentle Princes there

lines.text: Kind sister, thanks; we'll enter all together.
lines.plainText: Kind sister thanks we'll enter all together

lines.text: Right well, dear madam. By your patience,
lines.plainText: Right well dear madam By your patience

lines.text: I may not suffer you to visit them.
lines.plainText: I may not suffer you to visit them

lines.text: The King hath strictly charged the contrary.
lines.plainText: The King hath strictly charged the contrary

lines.text: The King? Who's that?
lines.plainText: The King Who's that

lines.text: I mean the Lord Protector.
lines.plainText: I mean the Lord Protector

lines.text: The Lord protect him from that kingly title!
lines.plainText: The Lord protect him from that kingly title

lines.text: Hath he set bounds between their love and me?
lines.plainText: Hath he set bounds between their love and me

lines.text: I am their mother; who shall bar me from them?
lines.plainText: I am their mother who shall bar me from them

lines.text: I am their father's mother. I will see them.
lines.plainText: I am their father's mother I will see them

lines.text: Their aunt I am in law, in love their mother.
lines.plainText: Their aunt I am in law in love their mother

lines.text: Then bring me to their sights. I'll bear thy blame,
lines.plainText: Then bring me to their sights I'll bear thy blame

lines.text: And take thy office from thee, on my peril.
lines.plainText: And take thy office from thee on my peril

lines.text: No, madam, no. I may not leave it so.
lines.plainText: No madam no I may not leave it so

lines.text: I am bound by oath, and therefore pardon me.
lines.plainText: I am bound by oath and therefore pardon me

lines.text: Let me but meet you, ladies, one hour hence,
lines.plainText: Let me but meet you ladies one hour hence

lines.text: And I'll salute your Grace of York as mother
lines.plainText: And I'll salute your Grace of York as mother

lines.text: And reverend looker-on of two fair queens.
lines.plainText: And reverend lookeron of two fair queens

lines.text: [To Anne.] Come, madam, you must straight to Westminster,
lines.plainText: To Anne Come madam you must straight to Westminster

lines.text: There to be crowned Richard's royal queen.
lines.plainText: There to be crowned Richard's royal queen

lines.text: Ah, cut my lace asunder
lines.plainText: Ah cut my lace asunder

lines.text: That my pent heart may have some scope to beat,
lines.plainText: That my pent heart may have some scope to beat

lines.text: Or else I swoon with this dead-killing news!
lines.plainText: Or else I swoon with this deadkilling news

lines.text: Despiteful tidings! O unpleasing news!
lines.plainText: Despiteful tidings O unpleasing news

lines.text: Be of good cheer, mother. How fares your Grace?
lines.plainText: Be of good cheer mother How fares your Grace

lines.text: O Dorset, speak not to me; get thee gone.
lines.plainText: O Dorset speak not to me get thee gone

lines.text: Death and destruction dog thee at thy heels;
lines.plainText: Death and destruction dog thee at thy heels

lines.text: Thy mother's name is ominous to children.
lines.plainText: Thy mother's name is ominous to children

lines.text: If thou wilt outstrip death, go, cross the seas,
lines.plainText: If thou wilt outstrip death go cross the seas

lines.text: And live with Richmond, from the reach of hell.
lines.plainText: And live with Richmond from the reach of hell

lines.text: Go, hie thee, hie thee from this slaughter-house,
lines.plainText: Go hie thee hie thee from this slaughterhouse

lines.text: Lest thou increase the number of the dead,
lines.plainText: Lest thou increase the number of the dead

lines.text: And make me die the thrall of Margaret's curse,
lines.plainText: And make me die the thrall of Margaret's curse

lines.text: Nor mother, wife, nor England's counted Queen.
lines.plainText: Nor mother wife nor England's counted Queen

lines.text: Full of wise care is this your counsel, madam.
lines.plainText: Full of wise care is this your counsel madam

lines.text: Take all the swift advantage of the hours;
lines.plainText: Take all the swift advantage of the hours

lines.text: You shall have letters from me to my son
lines.plainText: You shall have letters from me to my son

lines.text: In your behalf, to meet you on the way.
lines.plainText: In your behalf to meet you on the way

lines.text: Be not ta'en tardy by unwise delay.
lines.plainText: Be not ta'en tardy by unwise delay

lines.text: O ill-dispersing wind of misery!
lines.plainText: O illdispersing wind of misery

lines.text: O my accursed womb, the bed of death!
lines.plainText: O my accursed womb the bed of death

lines.text: A cockatrice hast thou hatched to the world,
lines.plainText: A cockatrice hast thou hatched to the world

lines.text: Whose unavoided eye is murderous.
lines.plainText: Whose unavoided eye is murderous

lines.text: Come, madam, come. I in all haste was sent.
lines.plainText: Come madam come I in all haste was sent

lines.text: And I with all unwillingness will go.
lines.plainText: And I with all unwillingness will go

lines.text: O, would to God that the inclusive verge
lines.plainText: O would to God that the inclusive verge

lines.text: Of golden metal that must round my brow
lines.plainText: Of golden metal that must round my brow

lines.text: Were red-hot steel, to sear me to the brains.
lines.plainText: Were redhot steel to sear me to the brains

lines.text: Anointed let me be with deadly venom,
lines.plainText: Anointed let me be with deadly venom

lines.text: And die ere men can say "God save the Queen."
lines.plainText: And die ere men can say God save the Queen

lines.text: Go, go, poor soul; I envy not thy glory.
lines.plainText: Go go poor soul I envy not thy glory

lines.text: To feed my humour, wish thyself no harm.
lines.plainText: To feed my humour wish thyself no harm

lines.text: No? Why? When he that is my husband now
lines.plainText: No Why When he that is my husband now

lines.text: Came to me as I followed Henry's corse,
lines.plainText: Came to me as I followed Henry's corse

lines.text: When scarce the blood was well washed from his hands
lines.plainText: When scarce the blood was well washed from his hands

lines.text: Which issued from my other angel husband,
lines.plainText: Which issued from my other angel husband

lines.text: And that dear saint which then I weeping followed;
lines.plainText: And that dear saint which then I weeping followed

lines.text: O, when, I say, I looked on Richard's face,
lines.plainText: O when I say I looked on Richard's face

lines.text: This was my wish: "Be thou," quoth I, "accursed
lines.plainText: This was my wish Be thou quoth I accursed

lines.text: For making me, so young, so old a widow;
lines.plainText: For making me so young so old a widow

lines.text: And when thou wedd'st, let sorrow haunt thy bed;
lines.plainText: And when thou wedd'st let sorrow haunt thy bed

lines.text: And be thy wife, if any be so mad,
lines.plainText: And be thy wife if any be so mad

lines.text: More miserable by the life of thee
lines.plainText: More miserable by the life of thee

lines.text: Than thou hast made me by my dear lord's death."
lines.plainText: Than thou hast made me by my dear lord's death

lines.text: Lo, ere I can repeat this curse again,
lines.plainText: Lo ere I can repeat this curse again

lines.text: Within so small a time, my woman's heart
lines.plainText: Within so small a time my woman's heart

lines.text: Grossly grew captive to his honey words,
lines.plainText: Grossly grew captive to his honey words

lines.text: And proved the subject of mine own soul's curse,
lines.plainText: And proved the subject of mine own soul's curse

lines.text: Which hitherto hath held my eyes from rest;
lines.plainText: Which hitherto hath held my eyes from rest

lines.text: For never yet one hour in his bed
lines.plainText: For never yet one hour in his bed

lines.text: Did I enjoy the golden dew of sleep,
lines.plainText: Did I enjoy the golden dew of sleep

lines.text: But with his timorous dreams was still awaked.
lines.plainText: But with his timorous dreams was still awaked

lines.text: Besides, he hates me for my father Warwick,
lines.plainText: Besides he hates me for my father Warwick

lines.text: And will, no doubt, shortly be rid of me.
lines.plainText: And will no doubt shortly be rid of me

lines.text: Poor heart, adieu; I pity thy complaining.
lines.plainText: Poor heart adieu I pity thy complaining

lines.text: No more than with my soul I mourn for yours.
lines.plainText: No more than with my soul I mourn for yours

lines.text: Farewell, thou woeful welcomer of glory.
lines.plainText: Farewell thou woeful welcomer of glory

lines.text: Adieu, poor soul, that tak'st thy leave of it.
lines.plainText: Adieu poor soul that tak'st thy leave of it

lines.text: [To Dorset.] Go thou to Richmond, and good fortune guide thee.
lines.plainText: To Dorset Go thou to Richmond and good fortune guide thee

lines.text: [To Anne.] Go thou to Richard, and good angels tend thee.
lines.plainText: To Anne Go thou to Richard and good angels tend thee

lines.text: [To Queen Elizabeth.] Go thou to sanctuary, and good thoughts possess thee.
lines.plainText: To Queen Elizabeth Go thou to sanctuary and good thoughts possess thee

lines.text: I to my grave, where peace and rest lie with me.
lines.plainText: I to my grave where peace and rest lie with me

lines.text: Eighty odd years of sorrow have I seen,
lines.plainText: Eighty odd years of sorrow have I seen

lines.text: And each hour's joy wracked with a week of teen.
lines.plainText: And each hour's joy wracked with a week of teen

lines.text: Stay, yet look back with me unto the Tower.
lines.plainText: Stay yet look back with me unto the Tower

lines.text: Pity, you ancient stones, those tender babes
lines.plainText: Pity you ancient stones those tender babes

lines.text: Whom envy hath immured within your walls—
lines.plainText: Whom envy hath immured within your walls

lines.text: Rough cradle for such little pretty one,
lines.plainText: Rough cradle for such little pretty one

lines.text: Rude ragged nurse, old sullen playfellow
lines.plainText: Rude ragged nurse old sullen playfellow

lines.text: For tender princes, use my babies well.
lines.plainText: For tender princes use my babies well

lines.text: So foolish sorrows bids your stones farewell.
lines.plainText: So foolish sorrows bids your stones farewell
